items.rationale: In a workflow, code predefines the path; in an agent, the model directs its own steps. Using tools, the number of model calls or the model size does not decide it.
The order is fixed in code, so it is a workflow even though it uses a tool and calls the model twice. Several model calls, tool use or self-checking do not make a system an agent.
The model picks each next step and the code only runs what it asks, which is what makes this an agent.
The steps are known and the same every time, so a workflow is cheaper and more predictable. The other tasks have open-ended or unpredictable steps, where an agent earns its cost.
The agent makes 8 - 3 = 5 extra calls per request: 5 x $0.002 = $0.01, and over 500 requests that is $5.
When the steps are known, a fixed workflow is cheaper and more predictable, and an agent's flexibility goes unused. Calling tools does not make a system an agent, and a workflow is not always better.
